reason: ux-reviewer triggers on "review this design/screen/flow/mock" and explicitly names the symptom — "a flow with more clicks than the job needs" whose leaner alternative it counter-proposes — so its description claims "onboarding flow ... feels heavy" more directly than design-critique's generic "usability, hierarchy, and consistency" feedback.
ux-copy's description literally lists "empty states" twice — "microcopy, error messages, empty states, CTAs" and "filling empty states" — which is exactly what the query asks for.

The description's trigger phrase "is this accessible?" is almost verbatim in the query, and it names "color contrast" as its review scope, which is precisely the grey-on-grey / blue-on-near-black concern.

user-research explicitly triggers on "interview guide" and "research questions" and covers research generally, whereas discovery-interview-prep scopes itself to *discovery* interviews and these are churn post-mortems, not discovery.

"does that hold up or am i overcomplicating it" maps onto ux-reviewer's stated trigger "is this the right design" plus its core job of catching over-built layouts and counter-proposing the leaner design; design-critique offers feedback but never claims the over-complication verdict.

Its trigger clause "reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow" plus "performance regressions" is satisfied literally by a connection pool exhausting under load, so I would fire it even though the user actually wants configuration tuning rather than a diagnosis loop.
